title: Anyone with a gym account can claim another gym's entry machine by typing its serial number first
what: A machine is added by typing the serial number printed on its label. The first gym to type a serial gets it for good; the server never asks for proof that the gym owns that machine. A rival gym, an ex-staff member with their own free gym, or a prankster who reads the label can add it first. The real gym is then told the machine is already added and cannot use it, and every door punch from that machine (member numbers and times) goes to the other gym. The 'already added' answer also tells anyone whether a serial is in use. Not live today: the entry machine service is written but not switched on.
expected: Adding a machine should prove the gym has it in hand (for example a code shown on the machine's screen or a setting typed into the machine), and a serial already claimed should be settled by support, not first come first served.
who: gyms with entry machines, once live
how_often: whenever someone learns a serial before the gym adds it
fix_line: Make adding a machine prove the gym holds it, before the service goes live

title: Entry machine check-ins are saved for any date, even years in the past or future
what: When a door machine sends its punches, each one carries the machine's own clock time. The server turns that into a visit for that day without checking it is near today. A machine whose clock reset after a power cut (often to the year 2000 or a wrong year), or anyone posing as the machine, can file visits on any day: old months fill with visits that never happened, and future days are already marked as attended, which feeds attendance numbers, the workout offer and challenge counts.
expected: A punch more than a day or two away from the server's own time is kept aside as 'machine clock looks wrong' and shown to the owner, not turned into a visit.
who: gyms with entry machines, once live
how_often: whenever a machine clock is wrong or a fake caller sends punches
fix_line: Refuse to make visits from punches far from today, and flag the machine's clock to the owner

title: Once the Pro gate is on, a Starter gym can open the Pro pages by blocking one check
what: The admin app asks the server once which pack the gym is on. If that answer does not arrive (offline, or blocked on purpose with a browser add-on), every Pro page opens. For most Pro parts the server will refuse new saves once its own gate is applied, but Your numbers is worked out in the browser and nothing on the server closes it, so a Starter gym gets it free for good by blocking one call. Not live: both gates are off today.
expected: Pages a Starter gym has not paid for stay closed when the pack is unknown for a gym that was already told it is on Starter, or Your numbers gets a server check like the other Pro parts.
who: Starter gyms, once the Pro gate is on
how_often: whenever an owner blocks the pack check
fix_line: Remember the last pack answer on the device and keep Pro pages closed when a known Starter gym's check fails
